names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 20 iunie, «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Metodie, Episcopul Patarelor»; the form is the bare name, the rest of the line being rank and see.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Ιουνίου, «Άγιος Μεθόδιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Πατάρων», with the rank words and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 20. јун ст. ст., „Свештеномученик Методије, епископ патарски“ — Свештеномученик is the rank and „епископ патарски“ is a second rank and the see, and §6 takes both off, as the folder’s Romanian and Greek notes already say in their own words. The bare forename is what is left and the heading offers nothing else. **The fold is deliberate and forced**: `foldchk.py` returns `methodius-of-constantinople` and `methodius-of-moravia`, both `sr`, for «Методије», so this is the third folder on the string, and the three are a patriarch, an apostle of the Slavs and this bishop of Patara. `corpus-gate.mjs` prints the row and a `READ_FOLDS` key is added for it in the same commit, writing the row and registering the fold being two acts.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 20 июня ст. ст., «Святитель Мефодий Патарский, Олимпийский, епископ, сщмч.», with the rank word, the see word and the grade word left off; both epithets are the calendar's own.

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's three other venerated rows carry. His life page life1353 heads «День памяти: 20 июня» and names no other day. That page gives the year of his death as 312, where this folder records 311; the dates were left as they stood and the disagreement is written into the life.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 июня ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Мефодия , еп. Патарского (312).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 20 iunie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Metodie, Episcopul Patarelor»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιος Μεθόδιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Πατάρων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 20 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. It is plainly the same man: the hieromartyr bishop of Patara, killed with a knife by a servant set on him by the Origenists he had driven back. The page prints no year in its own narrative, saying only «έζησε κατά τον 6ο μ.Χ. αιώνα», and then quotes S. Eustratiades against itself — that he flourished at the end of the third and the beginning of the fourth century, that according to Jerome and the historian Socrates he was bishop not of Patara but of Olympus in Lycia and afterwards of Tyre, that by another opinion he was bishop of Philippi in Macedonia, and that he was martyred at Chalcis in Syria under Diocletian. Because the page holds two irreconcilable datings and vouches for neither, no `dates` object is proposed here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.07.2026 (20. јун ст. ст.) — „Свештеномученик Методије, епископ патарски“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 20 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **A FIRST DATE ON A FOLDER THAT HELD `dates: null`, AND IT IS A FLAT YEAR.** Neither of the two books that made this folder gave a year of any kind. doxologia places the suffering in the reign of Aurelian and prints no year, and the folder’s own prose says so in as many words; saint.gr’s own account gives no year either, and only the opinion of S. Eustratiades which it sets against itself puts the death at Chalcis in Syria under Diocletian. This book states one year flat: „Незнабошци се дигоше на њега, мучише га и посекоше у Халкиди Сиријској 311. године“ — the pagans rose against him, tortured him and cut him down at Chalcis in Syria in the year 311. `death` 311 to 311, display «311», basis traditional. **NOTHING IS WIDENED AGAINST AURELIAN, BECAUSE A REIGN IS NOT A YEAR.** The standing rule refuses an emperor as a source for a year, so doxologia’s Aurelian is not a second reading to widen towards and the field is not «X or Y»: there is exactly one year on offer in three books and it is written flat. Nor is anything derived from the tension between Aurelian and this year; the disagreement is stated in the life and nowhere in a field. THE PLACE, AND WHICH BOOK OWNS IT. Chalcis in Syria is in the corpus already, but only as the **dissenting** opinion saint.gr prints against its own narrative of a murder by a planted servant — and **this book makes Chalcis its own account**, with a year attached, which is the first time the corpus holds it as a calendar’s own reading rather than as a scholar’s correction. No `locations` all the same: a place named once in a clause is not a coordinate, and the folder already carries Patara, Olympus, Tyre and Philippi in prose as four books’ four opinions about his see. WHAT ELSE IS NEW, AND IT IS LITTLE. „Из млада се посветио подвигу и као град на гори био виђен и позван на епископство“ — from his youth he gave himself to the ascetic struggle and, like a city on a hill, was seen and called to the episcopate, an image neither other book has. That he wrote **against the heresy of Origen** this book shares with doxologia, and its „богодухновене речи као муња засијаше по свему свету“ is doxologia’s own lightning sentence in Serbian, so two books now agree on it word for word. `ls saints | grep -i origen` holds only `leonides-father-of-origen`, and Origen himself is this entry’s heresiarch and no folder; **no rows at all** on this day. `types` UNTOUCHED, `office` UNTOUCHED. Свештеномученик is the `hieromartyr` and епископ the `bishop`, both of which the folder carries, and the `office` «Bishop» is already there; патарски is the see, which §6 keeps out of the stored form and which the folder’s own §10-reserved display name already carries. „Учен и красноречив архијереј“ — learned and eloquent — is in the body and would not have been written even had the corpus a type for it. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FIFTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети Левкије, епископ врунтисиопољски, у Италији“ — Leucius, born in Alexandria, early into a monastery, counted worthy of great revelations and of a mighty grace, so that he raised the dead and drove demons out of men; bishop first in Alexandria, then by a command from heaven crossing into Italy to the pagan city of Vruntisiopolj, which he baptised whole and in which he built a church of the Mother of God; and after much and successful labour passing over into eternity in the time of the emperor Theodosius II, in the fifth century. **Three folders hold the name and not one of them is he.** `ls saints | grep -i leuci` returns exactly three: `leucius-of-caesarea`, a martyr of 249–251 kept with Thyrsus and Coronatus, who is not a bishop and not of Italy; `leucius-companion-of-peter`, a martyr kept with Peter and Severus on the Greek 11 January; and `leucius-of-volokolamsk`, a Russian. `ls saints | grep -iE 'brundis|brindis'` returns nobody at all. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written on this day, and no folder from me — and **the fifth century, Theodosius II and the city are written nowhere**, because there is nothing to write them on. The day’s verse is his, and a verse is not a hymn and not a folder either. THE DAY’S SIXTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Блажени Студије“ — Studius, a notable patrician and consul in Constantinople, who founded near the Golden Gate the church of Saint John the Forerunner and the monastery called the Studion after him; a house that became famous for many glorious men, spiritual fathers, ascetics and sufferers for the faith; destroyed by the Latin crusaders in 1204, restored by the emperor Constantine Palaeologus Porphyrogenitus in 1293, and with a Turkish mosque standing on the place now. `ls saints | grep -i studi` returns five folders and **every one of them is a Studite and not the Studius the house is named after** — `damascene-the-studite`, `james-of-studion`, `naucratius-the-studite`, `nicholas-the-studite`, `theodore-the-studite`. The last of those is the man this entry names as the house’s most famous son, and **he takes no row and no mention in any prose written today**: a founder’s monastery is a dedication and a later inhabitant of it is not a relation. Ruling 3 on Studius himself: named here, no folder from me, and **1204, 1293 and the consulship are written nowhere**. The Блажени of his heading therefore decides nothing, there being no folder for it to decide a type on; had there been one it would still be the §5 reading «fool-for-christ *or* righteous — read which», and a patrician and consul who founds a monastery is neither obviously.

hymns.text: Şi părtaş obiceiurilor şi următor scaunelor apostolilor fiind, lucrare ai aflat, de Dumnezeu insuflate, spre suirea privirii la cele înalte. Pentru aceasta, cuvântul adevărului drept învăţând şi cu credinţa răbdând până la sânge Sfinţite Mucenice Metodie, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Metodie, Episcopul Patarelor, glasul 4; the text is the common of a hieromartyr, printed for him.

english.text: Having become a sharer of the apostles' ways and a successor to their thrones, thou didst find in action, O God-inspired one, an ascent to contemplation. Therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, and contending for the faith even unto blood, O Hieromartyr Methodius, intercede with Christ God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Ὡς στύλος ἀκλόνητος, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Χριστοῦ, καὶ λύχνος ἀείφωτος τῆς οἰκουμένης σοφέ, ἐδείχθης Μεθόδιε· ἔλαμψας ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, διὰ τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ἔλυσας τῶν εἰδώλων, τὴν σκοτόμαιναν μάκαρ, διὸ ἐν παρρησίᾳ Χριστῷ, πρέσβευε σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the first of two apolytikia on the page of «Άγιος Μεθόδιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Πατάρων», and it names him

english.text: You were shown, O wise Methodius, an unshaken pillar of the Church of Christ and an ever-shining lamp of the whole world; you gave light to the world by your martyrdom, and you broke the darkness of the idols, O blessed one. Therefore intercede boldly with Christ, that we may be saved.

hymns.text: Кровь твоя, мудре, тайно вопиет от земли,/ якоже Авелева к Богу,/ богомудре святителю Мефодие,/ ясно проповедавый Божие вочеловечение./ Темже и посрамил еси Оригенову лесть,/ и преставился еси в Небесный чертог./ Моли Христа Бога,// да спасет души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь священномученика Мефодия», глас 1. Proper to him: «богомудре святителю Мефодие» in the vocative, and it names Origen, whom his life page makes the heresy he fought.

english.text: Thy blood, O wise one, cries out secretly from the earth as Abel's did to God, hierarch Methodius wise in God, who didst plainly preach the becoming man of God. Therefore thou didst put Origen's deceit to shame, and didst pass over into the heavenly chamber. Pray to Christ God that He may save our souls.

hymns.text: Священнотаинник Святыя Троицы,/ и яже паче ума повелений Божественных проповедник,/ и православным утверждение был еси, Мефодие,/ злославныя обличил еси смыслы,/ правоверия ради кровию твоею священномученик явлься,/ и Христу со Ангелы предстоя,// моли спастися нам.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак священномученика Мефодия», глас 4. Proper to him: «Мефодие» in the vocative.

english.text: Thou wast a minister of the holy mysteries of the Trinity, a preacher of the divine commandments that are beyond understanding, and a strengthening of the Orthodox, O Methodius; thou didst reprove the minds of the ill-believing, and, being shown a hieromartyr by thy blood for the right faith, standing now before Christ with the angels, pray that we may be saved.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 20. јун ст. ст.: „Незнабошци се дигоше на њега, мучише га и посекоше у Халкиди Сиријској 311. године“ — the pagans rose against him, tortured him and cut him down at Chalcis in Syria in the year 311. The folder held no `dates` at all before this. doxologia places the suffering in the reign of Aurelian and prints no year; saint.gr gives no year in its own narrative and only the opinion it sets against itself, that of S. Eustratiades, puts the death at Chalcis in Syria under Diocletian. A reign is not a source for a year, so nothing is widened towards Aurelian and nothing is derived from the disagreement, which is stated in the life instead (5 October 2026).
